title: Patch-Seq Recording and Extraction Detailed Protocol
author: Brian Lee
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bw6gphbw
materials: Cascade Blue hydrazide, Trisodium Salt (Invitrogen C687)
Nextera XT DNA Sample Preparation Kit (Illumina FC-131-1096).

steps.title: Prepare EGTA Stock Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a 192 mM EGTA stock solution in an RNase-free hood.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 3.65 g of EGTA in 32 ml nuclease-free water in a 50 ml conical tube.
Add 1 N KOH dropwise until dissolved (up to 10 ml).
Bring final volume to 50 ml with nuclease-free water.
Store at 4 °C for up to 60 days.

steps.title: Prepare Fluor Dye Stock
steps.instruction: Prepare a ~10 mM fluorophore stock solution.

substeps.instruction: Add 175 µl of nuclease-free water to 1 mg of desired dye in a 1.5 ml LoBind tube.
Aliquot 25 µl into PCR strips.
Label with expiration date and store at -20 °C for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Prepare Internal Stock Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 80 ml of internal stock solution in an RNase-free hood using a glass beaker on a stir plate.

substeps.instruction: Wipe surfaces with RNase AWAY/RNaseZap and 70% EtOH.
Measure 60 ml nuclease-free water into a glass beaker containing an RNase-free stir bar.
Place beaker in a mixture of wet and dry ice on a stir plate; stir at setting 7 or higher.

Slowly add the following while stirring: 2.06 g K-gluconate, 160 µl 2 M KCl, 800 µl 1 M HEPES, 40.56 mg ATP-Mg, 12.56 mg GTP-Na, 204.08 mg sodium phosphocreatine, 400 mg biocytin, 82 µl 192 mM EGTA stock, and 80 µl 20 mg/ml glycogen solution.
Stir at high speed until fully dissolved (< 1 minute).
Adjust pH to 7.3 using 1 N KOH in 40 µl increments; discard if target is overshot.
Remove stir bar and adjust final volume to 78 ml with nuclease-free water.
Measure osmolarity (10 µl sample); adjust to 220-230 mOsm using nuclease-free water (if too high) or K-gluconate in µg increments (if too low).
Filter through a Steriflip 0.22 µm filter system attached to a Gast vacuum pump.

steps.title: Aliquot and Store Internal Stock
steps.instruction: Aliquot the filtered internal stock solution for long-term storage.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot into 10 ml quantities (or as needed) and label with expiration date.
Store 5 ml aliquots at -80 °C for up to 60 days.

steps.title: Prepare Final Internal Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the final working internal solution from a thawed 10 ml aliquot of internal stock every two weeks.

substeps.instruction: Add 125 µl RNase inhibitor (40 U/µl) and 50 µl fluorophore stock (~10 mM) to 10 ml of internal solution.
Transfer 500 µl of solution into 20 Millipore centrifugal filters; spin at 200x g for 3 minutes. Repeat with fresh filters.
Verify final osmolarity is ~330-335 mOsm using a 10 µl sample.
Aliquot 200 µl into 1.5 ml LoBind tubes and store at -80 °C.

steps.title: Validate Internal Solution
steps.instruction: Test new batches for contamination before use.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 µl of internal solution to a 'blank' and process for Smarter reaction.
Examine Bioanalyzer traces; discard batch if amplifiable content is detected.

steps.title: Prepare Collection Buffer Blanks
steps.instruction: Prepare lysis buffer blanks for sample collection.

substeps.instruction: Combine SMART-Seq v4 lysis buffer (0.83x concentration), RNase Inhibitor (0.17 U/µl), and ERCCs (MIX1 at 1x10-8).
Fill 0.2 ml PCR tubes with 10.4 µl of collection buffer and store at -80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Brain Slices
steps.instruction: Prepare mouse or human brain slices and allow them to rest in incubation ACSF for at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Set Up Workspace and Rig
steps.instruction: Prepare the laminar flow hood and electrophysiology rig.

substeps.instruction: Wipe ice buckets and 96-well plates with DNA AWAY, RNase AWAY/RNaseZap, and nuclease-free water; wipe hoods with 70% ethanol.
Fill one ice bucket with wet ice (for lysis buffer blanks) and two with dry ice (for internal solution and samples).
Wipe headstage and pipette holder with DNA AWAY, RNase AWAY/RNaseZap, and nuclease-free water; wipe electrode wire with nuclease-free water only.
Wipe desk area with 70% ethanol.
Perfuse oxygenated recording ACSF at 2 mL/min for ~10 minutes; maintain chamber temperature at 34 ± 1 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Pipettes
steps.instruction: Pull and prepare filamented pipettes using a Narishige PC-10.

substeps.instruction: Aim for resistance of 3.5-5 MΩ; pull no more than three pairs at a time.
Store in a closed box and pull fresh daily.
Set micromanipulator approach angle to 30°.

steps.title: Position Tissue and Select Cell
steps.instruction: Transfer and position the brain slice in the recording chamber.

substeps.instruction: Transfer slice to chamber using a transfer pipet with the tip cut off.
Position tissue in the center using a clean paintbrush or closed forceps.
Place the harp on top of the slice over the region of interest.
Select a healthy cell (plump, smooth, not shriveled/blown out). If fluorescently labeled, ensure it is clearly defined with visible dendrites.
Wipe electrode wire with Kimwipe and nuclease-free water.
Fill glass pipette with 1-2 µl of internal solution using a 20 µl pipette and fresh microloader tip; eliminate bubbles.
Attach pipette to headstage; apply 30-70 mbar positive pressure and insert into bath (resistance 3.5-5 MΩ).
Bring pipette above slice; apply ~70 mbar positive pressure and set pipette offset to 60-80 mV.
Approach cell; press tip until a dimple appears or access resistance increases by ≥ 0.2 MΩ, then quickly release positive pressure.
Apply holding voltage (eventually -70 mV) and negative pressure to achieve a GΩ seal.
Use Auto Cp Fast to compensate for pipette capacitance.
Break into the cell using small bursts of negative pressure (-50 to -150 mbar) and/or zap (starting at 25 µs).
Verify access resistance is < 20 MΩ and < 15% of input resistance; apply < 10 mbar suction if needed to combat swelling.
Perform area-specific acquisition protocols.

steps.title: Extract Cytosol and Nucleus
steps.instruction: Extract the cytosol and nucleus upon completion of electrophysiology.

substeps.instruction: Position pipette near the nucleus (visible as a dark circle under fluorescent filter or the plumpest part of the cell).
Slowly apply negative pressure (-30 to -50 mbar) while monitoring soma shape and membrane stability.
If membrane destabilizes, release pressure, stabilize, and retry.
If nucleus is sucked in, immediately release pressure and proceed to retraction.

steps.title: Retract Pipette
steps.instruction: Retract the pipette to obtain a nucleated patch.

substeps.instruction: Re-center pipette on the nucleus and nudge against the edge of the nucleus.
With continued negative pressure, move pipette tip toward the membrane edge; switch to diagonal mode.
Pull out very slowly (≤ 1 µm/sec), pausing at intervals to let the membrane relax.
If access resistance increases, re-position against the nucleus and increase negative pressure.
Continue retracting until fully removed from the slice. If post-seal resistance is > 1000 MΩ, retraction speed can be increased.
If post-seal resistance is < 1 GΩ but nucleus is attached, increase negative pressure to suck in the nucleus, then release immediately.

steps.title: Expel Contents into Lysis Buffer
steps.instruction: Expel the cytosol and nucleus into a collection buffer tube.

substeps.instruction: Remove pipette from bath and detach from holder.
Insert pipette into expulsion device and tighten screw.
Apply 10-20 mbar positive pressure (displace 0.05-0.1 ml of a 1 ml syringe).
Submerge pipette tip into a PCR tube containing collection buffer; break off a small piece of the tip against the wall/bottom.
Allow contents to drain and raise pipette as it empties.
Spin down tube for 5 seconds at ~6000 rpm.
Label and flash freeze in a metal 96-well plate on dry ice; store at -80 °C.

steps.title: Perform RNA Amplification
steps.instruction: Amplify RNA using the Takara SMART-Seq v4 Ultra Low Input RNA Kit.

substeps.instruction: Check Alexa fill quality via fluorescent filter for rapid feedback.
Follow manufacturer instructions for SMART-Seq v4 at 1x, using 20 PCR cycles for patched nuclei.
Prepare 88 sample tubes and a control strip (containing NTC, 10 pg Whole Mouse Brain Total RNA, and 10 pg Control RNA) on ice.
Purify amplification product via bead cleanup (1x ratio) with 17 µl elution volume (10mM Tris-Cl, pH 8.5).

steps.title: Quality Control of Amplification
steps.instruction: Analyze the amplification product using a Fragment Analyzer and PicoGreen.

substeps.instruction: Quantify sizing and yield using HS NGS Fragment Kit.
Pass criteria: > 50% of product in 400-6000 bp range; yield > 7000 pg.
Fail criteria: < 40% of product in 400-6000 bp range; yield < 6000 pg (if trace is absent).
Verify PG/FA yield ratio is between 0.80 and 1.20.

steps.title: Prepare Sequencing Library
steps.instruction: Prepare the library using the Nextera XT DNA Sample Preparation Kit.

substeps.instruction: Normalize cDNA concentration to 50 pg/µl using Nuclease-Free Water.
Use 0.2x of the volumes instructed in the manufacturer's protocol for input and reagents.
Index libraries using custom 10-base unique dual-index primers (2 µl of 2.5 µM forward and reverse primers combined).
Purify library product via bead cleanup (0.9x ratio) with 22 µl elution volume (10mM Tris-Cl, pH 8.5).

steps.title: Library Quality Control and Pooling
steps.instruction: Validate the library and pool samples for sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Quantify sizing and concentration via HS NGS Fragment Kit; average size should be ~300 bp, concentration ~1.5 ng/µl.
Verify PG/FA yield ratio is between 0.80 and 1.20.
Normalize 5 µl of library product to 4-8 nM using Nuclease-Free Water.
Pool 2 µl from each sample in a 96-index set (total 192 µl) at 2-10 nM.
Further multiplex 8x96 libraries with compatible index sets for Illumina NovaSeqS2-XP (~500K PE50 reads per sample).
